a.head: Understand the universe. Start with curiosity.
a.intro: Horizonte is a place to learn about the universe, physics and engineering. Explore real NASA images, find free learning activities and sources, and discover the educational materials we are developing.
a.routes: Choose what you want to learn.
a.physicsText: Observe an archive image. What was measured and what is an interpretation? Compare its description with the original source.
a.engineeringText: Choose a real mission. Note its goal, instruments and constraints. How would its design change with less energy or more distance?
a.fictionText: Choose a question about space. Compare two sources, separate observations from hypotheses and note what the evidence supports.
a.free: Free resources · External sources in English
a.shopIntro: We are designing original resources and objects for people who look up. These concepts are in development and are not yet for sale.
a.guideText: Original digital workbooks with learning paths, exercises and annotated references.
a.kitText: A concept for guided science and engineering activities to do at home.
a.merchText: Educational prints, notebooks and T-shirts with original designs from our brand.

l.title: Light takes time to arrive.
l.intro: Read, experiment and solve the challenge here on Horizonte. Progress lasts for this visit to the page.
l.explain: A light-year measures distance: the path light travels in a vacuum in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres. If an object's light takes four years to reach us, we see it as it was when that light left.
l.result: Light takes {years} years to travel this distance.
l.model: Teaching model: stationary source and observer, light in a vacuum. It does not simulate cosmic expansion or spacecraft travel.
l.challenge: Challenge: a light signal leaves a source 8 light-years away. When does it arrive?
l.speed: It depends on the spacecraft's speed
l.correct: Correct! You are calculating light's journey: 8 light-years correspond to 8 years of light travel in this model.
l.retry: Not yet. The signal travels at light speed, not spacecraft speed. A light-year is the distance light travels in one year. Try again.
